prompt: In many countries woman no longer feel the need to get married. Some people believe that this is because women are able to earn their own income and therefore do not require financial security that marriage can bring. To what extend do you agree?
essay:
In many parts of the world, marriage is no longer something women consider essential. This is often attributed to their ability to support themselves financially, meaning they no longer depend on a husband for security. I agree that fewer women are choosing to marry, but I believe loneliness and the difficulty of finding a suitable partner are the stronger reasons.

Loneliness has become far more common in recent years, and I believe social media is a major cause. It raises expectations of what a partner should be, while also damaging people's self-esteem, so they become dissatisfied with what they have or with themselves. People only see a small part of someone's life online, and those who appear happiest may be just as lonely behind the camera. Over time this can contribute to depression, particularly for those who do not seek professional help.

Women hold far more jobs today than in the 1950s, when they had few opportunities outside the home and were expected to raise children and manage the household. Women nowadays are able to earn their own money so they no longer need a husband for financial security. However, financial independence alone does not explain the change, since many women who earn well still want a partner and simply cannot find one.

In conclusion, I partly agree that financial independence has reduced the need to marry, but I believe it is not the main cause. Rising loneliness and the difficulty of finding a suitable partner explain the change far better.
